title: Can not modify the proxy server
body: I run code-server in a Docker container listening on port 20000, mapped to host port 62400. nginx 1.24.0 listens on port 20015, and I access code-server at https://host-ip:20015/62400/. The IDE loads, but changing its theme has no effect. My regex location proxies `/<port>/<path>` with `proxy_pass http://0.0.0.0:$1/$2;`. The nginx access log shows the theme resource request, including its `path` and `tkn` query parameters, receiving status 400.

symptoms_visible: I can open code-server at https://host-ip:20015/62400/, but changing the IDE theme has no effect.
The theme resource request has `path` and `tkn` parameters in the browser-facing URL and receives a 400 response.
N0.label: N0 code-server theme request fails through nginx

symptoms_visible: The IDE opens through nginx, but I cannot set the theme or use keyboard shortcuts.
The theme works when I access code-server without nginx.
N1.label: N1 failure isolated to nginx path

symptoms_visible: The theme resource still returns 400 through nginx, and I do not know how to obtain the complete text request.
N2.label: N2 complete request unavailable

symptoms_visible: The theme request still receives 400 through nginx.
My debug log records the incoming request line with the `path` and empty `tkn` arguments and a Host header for port 20015.
N3.label: N3 debug request evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After updating the proxy configuration to pass the original query string, changing the code-server theme through nginx works.
N_terminal.label: terminal query string preserved and theme works

question_patterns: Can you show what happens when you try to change the theme?
Could you share a screenshot of the failed theme change?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached a screenshot. I can access the IDE, but I cannot set the theme. I also cannot use keyboard shortcuts, and the theme works if I do not use nginx.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same theme failure happens when I connect directly without nginx.
The IDE appearance differs slightly, but the same theme resource receives 400 only through nginx.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1, c4 and c5 on the reporter's own setup: the screenshot illustrates the failure, keyboard shortcuts are also affected, and bypassing nginx removes the theme problem.

question_patterns: Can you share the complete failing request in text form?
Could you capture and paste all headers and the complete request rather than only a screenshot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sorry, I don't know how to get the complete request.

edges.comment: Participant request c6/c8 and reporter response c9: the reporter could not capture the complete request directly, leading to the debug-log measurement instead.

question_patterns: Could you enable nginx debug logging, reproduce the request, and paste the relevant error-log section?
Please reproduce the problem with debug logging enabled and share the request and upstream-response lines.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here are the debug logs. They include `GET /62400/stable-08cbdfbdf11925e8a14ee03de97b942bba7e8a94/vscode-remote-resource?path=%2Froot%2Fcode-server%2Fcode-server-4.96.2-linux-amd64%2Flib%2Fvscode%2Fextensions%2Ftheme-defaults%2Fthemes%2Fdark_vs.json&tkn= HTTP/1.1`, `http args: "path=...dark_vs.json&tkn="`, and `Host: 10.222.20.23:20015`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug log shows nginx itself rejecting the request before selecting or contacting an upstream.
The same request and arguments appear with a different client port and timestamp.

edges.comment: Participant instruction c10 and reporter log c11 on the reporter's nginx instance. The answer contains only pasted request evidence; participant1's later conclusion that nginx accepted it and the upstream returned 400 is engineer-side interpretation.

solution.intent: Preserve the original request query string when proxy_pass constructs the upstream URI from regex captures by appending `$is_args$args`, then have the user reproduce the theme change and verify the upstream no longer returns 400.
solution.concrete_example: Change the directive to `proxy_pass http://0.0.0.0:$1/$2$is_args$args;`, reload nginx, and retry changing the theme. Confirm that the theme resource succeeds instead of returning 400.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the configured proxy_pass, the incoming request with its query parameters, the 400 result, and the debug request evidence. Inferring that constructing a replacement URI from `$1/$2` omitted the original query string—and that the upstream therefore rejected the resource request—was participant2's diagnosis, confirmed when `$is_args$args` fixed the problem.

edges.comment: Participant2 proposal c15 and reporter confirmation c16-c17 on the reporter's system: appending `$is_args$args` to proxy_pass fixed the problem. The terminal state represents the persistent nginx configuration change and the reporter's confirmation.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the regex proxy_pass constructed a replacement upstream URI without preserving the original query string, so code-server received an incomplete resource request and returned 400.
Must ground the diagnosis in the configured `$1/$2` proxy_pass, the incoming request's `path` and `tkn` arguments, the debug log, and the fact that direct access without nginx works.
Must fix the proxy by preserving the query string, for example with `proxy_pass http://0.0.0.0:$1/$2$is_args$args;`.
Must not settle on an invalid client request or missing Host header: the debug log contains a valid request line, arguments, and Host header, while the 400 comes from the upstream path.
Must ask the user to reload nginx and verify that the theme operation succeeds through nginx before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical operator who can build nginx, configure a regex reverse proxy, run Docker port mappings, enable debug logging, and paste logs, but does not know how to capture a complete HTTP request independently.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, cooperative, and informal; corrects mistakes directly, shares requested evidence, and enthusiastically confirms when a configuration change works.
